user_access_token.description: Standard user-facing API access token — minimal claims for authorization
notes: typ: at+jwt per RFC 9068 (JWT access token profile)
sub: opaque user ID, not email/username
aud: specific API audience, not wildcard
exp: 15 minutes from iat (900 seconds)
jti: unique token ID for revocation checks
No PII in claims — use userinfo endpoint for profile data

service_to_service.description: Machine-to-machine token via client credentials grant
notes: sub matches client_id for service identity
Shorter expiry (5 min) — services can refresh easily
Narrow scope — only what this service needs
No user context (no act claim) — pure service call

delegated_token.description: Token exchange result — service acting on behalf of user
notes: sub: original user (resource owner)
act: the service performing the action (delegation chain)
Scope narrowed from original token
Audience changed to downstream service
Enables audit trail: who did what, on whose behalf
cnf.jkt: SHA-256 thumbprint of client's DPoP public key
token_type: DPoP (not Bearer) — RS must verify proof
Stolen token is useless without client's private key
Use for high-value APIs (banking, admin, data export)

multi_tenant_token.description: Token for multi-tenant SaaS with organization context
notes: org_id: tenant isolation — enforce at API AND database layer
org_role: role within the organization context
permissions: pre-computed at token issuance for fast checks
User may have different roles in different orgs — token is org-scoped
RLS policy: WHERE org_id = token.org_id on all queries
